lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.title: Skill model: timeline with verified dates and requirements

objective: Learners practice distinguishing a date or requirement they have verified from a real, checkable source from one they are only assuming, then build a timeline for their leading pathway using verified information, with any remaining assumptions clearly flagged rather than treated as fact.
scenario: Given a short model timeline where some entries are already labeled 'verified' (with a source noted) and others are labeled 'assumed,' the learner studies how each label was decided, then applies the same process to build a timeline for their own leading pathway.
safetyNotes: No real account numbers, passwords, or legal identity details are needed to complete this lesson.
materials: notes on the learner's leading pathway from earlier units
paper or a document for the timeline

tasks.directions: Before looking at the model, list dates or requirements you currently believe are true about your leading pathway.

prompts.text: Name two dates or requirements you currently believe are true about your pathway, and be honest about whether you've actually checked them anywhere or are just assuming.

tasks.directions: Study the model timeline and identify what makes an entry count as 'verified' versus 'assumed.'

prompts.text: In the model timeline, what specifically makes an entry 'verified' rather than 'assumed' — what counts as a real, checkable source?

I can name at least one source (such as an official program page, a published catalog, or a direct answer from someone at the institution or organization) that would count as verification, not just a guess or something a peer said.

tasks.directions: Build a timeline of at least four dates or requirements for your own leading pathway, labeling each as verified (with the source) or assumed.

prompts.text: List at least four dates or requirements for your leading pathway. For each, write whether it is verified or assumed, and if verified, name the source.
Every entry in my timeline is labeled either 'verified' with a real source, or 'assumed.'

tasks.directions: Reflect on what to do about the entries still marked assumed.

prompts.text: Pick one entry you marked 'assumed.' What specific, doable step would move it to 'verified,' and roughly when could you take that step?

remediation: If a learner labels something 'verified' without naming a real, specific, checkable source (for example, writing 'verified' but citing only 'I think I heard'), reteach the distinction directly: model one clear verified example with its exact source named, one clear assumed example, and have the learner re-sort their own timeline entries into the correct category before moving forward.
extension: Have the learner identify which single assumed entry, if wrong, would most disrupt the rest of the timeline, and write a short plan for verifying that one first.
